\section{Overview}

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Signed value of a query check]
\lean{FABL.e3LinCheckSignedValue}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p185-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p186-b001
}
\label{FABL.e3LinCheckSignedValue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BoundedCubeFunction.ofBoolean, FABL.SignQueryCheck, FABL.SignQueryCheck.randomizedValue}
Given a sign-valued Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube and a sign
query check $C$, let $v$ be the randomized acceptance probability of $C$ when applied to
the bounded real-valued cube function corresponding to $f$. The signed value of the
check is $2v-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Signed value of a linearity check]
\lean{FABL.e3LinCheckSignedValue_eq}
\label{FABL.e3LinCheckSignedValue_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.Sign, FABL.SignQueryCheck, FABL.SignQueryCheck.randomizedValue, FABL.e3LinCheckSignedValue, FABL.e3LinPredicate, FABL.e3LinPredicate_randomizedValue, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $C$ be a check with three queries into the sign cube
$\{-1,1\}^n$, let $b\in\{-1,1\}$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. If the predicate
used by $C$ accepts precisely those triples whose product equals $b$, then the signed
value of the randomized check on $f$ is
\[b\prod_{j=0}^{2} f(C_j),\]
where $C_j$ denotes the query at position $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Odd parity factorization]
\lean{FABL.e3LinCheckSignedValue_oddParity}
\label{FABL.e3LinCheckSignedValue_oddParity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignQueryCheck, FABL.dictator, FABL.dictator_toReal_eq_monomial_singleton, FABL.e3LinCheckSignedValue, FABL.e3LinCheckSignedValue_eq, FABL.maxE3LinPredicates, FABL.monomial, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.parityFunction_toReal, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer and let $C$ be a sign-query check on $2k+1$ coordinates
whose predicate accepts exactly when the product of its three input signs equals some
fixed sign. The signed value of $C$ on the parity of all $2k+1$ coordinates equals the
product, over all coordinates $i$, of its signed values on the individual coordinate
functions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Attaining the maximum on the support of a probability mass function]
\lean{FABL.eq_one_on_pmf_support}
\label{FABL.eq_one_on_pmf_support}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\\Omega$ be a finite set, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\\Omega$, and
let $g:\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R$ satisfy $g(x)\\le 1$ for every $x$. If the expectation of
$g$ under $p$ is $1$, then $g(x)=1$ at every point with $p(x)\\ne 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Upper bound for signed acceptance value]
\lean{FABL.e3LinCheckSignedValue_le_one}
\label{FABL.e3LinCheckSignedValue_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BoundedCubeFunction.ofBoolean, FABL.SignQueryCheck, FABL.SignQueryCheck.randomizedValue_mem_Icc, FABL.e3LinCheckSignedValue}
\difficulty{3}
For any sign-query check $C$ and Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube,
the signed value $2R-1$ is at most $1$, where $R$ is the check's randomized acceptance
value on $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Perfect acceptance gives signed value one]
\lean{FABL.expect_e3LinCheckSignedValue_eq_one}
\label{FABL.expect_e3LinCheckSignedValue_eq_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BoundedCubeFunction.ofBoolean, FABL.SignQueryCheck.randomizedValue, FABL.SignTester, FABL.SignTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.e3LinCheckSignedValue, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be a finite random-seed tester and let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign
cube. If the tester's acceptance probability on $f$ is $1$, then the average over its
seed distribution of the signed value of its selected check on $f$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}

Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer and let $T$ be a sign tester on $2k+1$ coordinates.
Suppose every check of $T$ uses a predicate accepting exactly when the product of three
input signs equals a fixed sign, and $T$ accepts each individual coordinate function
with probability $1$. Then $T$ accepts the parity of all $2k+1$ coordinates with
probability $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Impossibility of perfect-completeness testing]
\lean{FABL.no_maxE3Lin_dictatorVsNoNotables_of_perfectCompleteness}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b004}
\label{FABL.no_maxE3Lin_dictatorVsNoNotables_of_perfectCompleteness}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BoundedCubeFunction.ofBoolean, FABL.HasSmallStableInfluences, FABL.IsDictatorVsNoNotablesTest, FABL.SignTester, FABL.SignTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.SignTester.acceptanceProbability_mem_Icc, FABL.dictator, FABL.e3LinTester_accepts_oddParity_of_accepts_dictators, FABL.maxE3LinPredicates, FABL.monomial, FABL.monomial_hasSmallStableInfluences_of_card, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.parityFunction_toReal}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\alpha<1$. There do not exist an error function $\lambda:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and
a family of randomized finite-query testers, one for each positive dimension, with all
of the following properties: each tester uses only predicates that accept triples of
signs exactly when their product equals a fixed sign; its predicate family is finite;
and for some acceptance threshold $\beta=1$, one has $0<\alpha<\beta\le1$. The error
values lie in $[0,1]$ for inputs in $[0,1]$ and tend to $0$ as the input decreases to
$0$ through positive values. Every dictator (the function returning one chosen
coordinate) is accepted with probability at least $\beta$, while every function whose
stable influence at each coordinate is at most $\varepsilon$ is accepted with
probability at most $\alpha+\lambda(\varepsilon)$, for every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$.
\end{theorem}
